A pinned sense narrower than the defined sense is judged on the pinned sense, and that sense fails its own test: the spectrogram was not built and maintained for audio engineering practice. It is a general analysis display — developed in radio/radar spectrum work, and used in speech science, sonar, bioacoustics, and acoustics alongside audio engineering. SERVES asks 'built for whose sake?'; there is no single master here, so the edge misattributes a general tool to one consuming discipline.

The accepted definition carves a windowing function as a family of closed-form functions that taper a signal segment to reduce spectral leakage in DFT analysis, 'instantiated as numerical coefficients in DSP software and signal processing libraries.' It is maintained as a general digital-signal-processing construct, not for audio engineering. The note's 'built and maintained for audio engineering practice' is false on the defined sense: windows are the general toolkit of spectral estimation across radar, communications, seismology, and audio alike. 'For whose sake' has no single answer; audio engineering is one consumer among many. STRIKE.

Direction holds on independent historical reasoning. The sankey diagram (P.A.J. Sankey, 1861) established the encoding of flow magnitude as proportional ribbon width; the alluvial diagram (web/D3 era, early 2010s) reuses exactly that encoding — its own accepted definition describes ribbon flows whose widths are proportional to flow volume between ordered stages — repurposed for categorical transitions. Which-came-first: sankey precedes alluvial by ~150 years; what-fed-into: the width-proportional ribbon encoding is the direct lineage. The note's attribution is sloppy (it says 'Matthew Sankey in 1898'; the inventor was P.A.J. Sankey, 1861), but the error does not reverse direction: even on the note's own wrong date, sankey still predates alluvial by a century-plus. ADVANCE.

payload.body: Silence is a conceptual category marking the absence or suppression of sound, speech, or communication within a defined context. Its parameters are the domain (acoustic, discursive, legal, or social) and the agent (intentional or circumstantial). It persists through cultural conventions, legal statutes (e.g., right to silence), and social norms that define when quiet is meaningful versus merely absent. [formal: silentium | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Agency is the conceptual category for the capacity of an entity to act with intentionality and causal influence within a domain. Its parameters are the agent (individual, collective, or system), the domain of influence (physical, social, computational), and the degree of constraint. It persists through legal frameworks (rights, duties), philosophical discourse, and everyday language that distinguishes agents from instruments or passive phenomena. [formal: agenticitas | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Intent is the conceptual category for a mental state that directs action toward a specific goal or outcome. Its parameters are the agent (conscious or attributed), the specificity of the goal, and the temporal horizon over which the goal is maintained. It persists through language (verbs of purpose, legal standards of intent), moral frameworks that attribute responsibility, and legal systems that distinguish intentional from negligent conduct. [formal: intentio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Loss is the conceptual category marking the transition from possession or presence to absence or unavailability of something valued. Its parameters are the domain (material, relational, temporal, or informational), the mode (sudden or gradual, expected or unexpected), and the agent's relationship to the lost item (owner, witness, or affected party). It persists through language (grief vocabulary, accounting standards, insurance frameworks), social rituals (mourning, bankruptcy proceedings), and cultural narratives that give shape to absence. [formal: amissio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
